title: OAB Capacity Result
description: The output of one capacity calculation. Every calculation is reproducible: same inputs, same numbers, from a tested implementation. The envelope is fixed so a reader can check the arithmetic by hand and dispute a specific line rather than the conclusion.

calculator.description: Which calculator produced this, e.g. 'rps' or 'storage_growth'.

assumptions.description: Every input, labelled by where it came from. An empty list is impossible: even a fully observed calculation has assumptions about what the observation means.

source.description: observed = measured from the system; stated = the user said so; assumed = OAB filled a gap; calculated = derived from an earlier result.

impact_if_wrong.description: How much the result moves if this input is wrong, e.g. '±3x on RPS'.

formula.description: The literal expression, in symbols, so it can be disputed independently of the numbers.

calculation.description: The formula with values substituted, so a reader can check it by hand. This is what makes the result auditable rather than trusted.

range.description: Required whenever any input has low confidence. A point estimate from an uncertain input is false precision.

significant_figures.description: At most 2 for any value derived from an assumed input. '0.28 RPS' is honest; '0.2777 RPS' is a lie about precision.

rationale.description: Why this margin. A margin without a reason is superstition.

confidence.description: Propagated, not asserted: a chain containing any low-confidence input cannot report high confidence. Note that confidence in the DECISION can still be high when the result is insensitive to every uncertain input across its plausible range — that case is stated in `sensitivity`.

dominant_input.description: Which single assumption most changes the result — the one to go and measure first.

decision_is_insensitive.description: True when the conclusion holds across the entire plausible input range. This is a stronger finding than any individual number and should be stated plainly when it holds.
